notes: Added town (Tarkhanewala-Dera, District Ganganagar, Rajasthan; Mature Harappan structures excavated 2003-04 under the Sarasvati Heritage Project). Plans only. The walls are drawn as rows of outlined mud bricks, so each line is an edge fitted on the cleanest outer outline of a wall. On Fig. 4 most walls (Str. 7A, 7C, 7E, 8, 10A, 5B) lie within -1.1 to +4.3 degrees of the plan arrow (system main); the long Str. 17 in the eastern trenches lies at -5.0 and Str. 5D at +8.7. On Fig. 5 (Str. 19A-C, 20A-B) all walls lie at -4.2 to -7.7 relative to that plan's own arrow, and Str. 19 and Str. 20 are 3 degrees from perpendicular. The walls of both plans form rectilinear houses turned close to the cardinal directions of the plan arrows; the two plans' arrows were drawn separately, so their relative offset is not known. Bricks are drawn individually and the walls are short (1.6-5.7 m), so drafting irregularity dominates over the fit sigma.
